stem: Which TCP port does SSH use by default for management sessions?
explanation: SSH listens on TCP 22. Because it is TCP, a completed three-way handshake proves the listener is reachable before any key exchange begins, which is why a firewall rule that permits 22 but blocks the return path fails during handshake rather than at the banner.

stem: Which command restricts a Cisco router to SSH version 2 only?
explanation: `ip ssh version 2` disables the older version 1 negotiation, so every client must use the current protocol. Version 1 has known weaknesses in its integrity checking, and leaving it enabled means a client can silently downgrade the session.

stem: Which VTY line configuration makes the router check incoming SSH credentials against usernames stored in its own configuration?
explanation: `login local` tells the line to authenticate against the local user database created with `username`, instead of the line password. That is what makes per-user credentials and privilege levels possible on SSH sessions.

stem: Which command shows the SSH protocol version, authentication timeout, and retry count in effect on a Cisco router?
explanation: `show ip ssh` reports the version, the authentication timeout, and the number of retries, which is exactly the set of values to confirm after tightening a management policy. Connection-level detail belongs to `show ssh`, which lists active sessions.

stem: What does a VLAN access map (VACL) filter that a normal router ACL cannot?
explanation: A VACL is applied to a VLAN rather than an interface, so it filters traffic between ports in the same VLAN, including traffic that never leaves the switch. A router ACL only sees traffic that is routed through the device.

choices.text: Traffic switched between ports inside the same VLAN, without being routed
Traffic entering the router's WAN interface
Only broadcast and multicast frames on trunk links
Only packets generated by the switch's own management process

stem: What does a private VLAN provide inside a single IP subnet?
explanation: Private VLANs split one VLAN into isolated and community subdomains with a promiscuous uplink port. Hosts on isolated ports can reach only the promiscuous port, which is how a provider stops customers in the same subnet from talking to each other.

choices.text: Port-level isolation between hosts that still share one subnet and default gateway
A second default gateway for redundancy inside the same VLAN
Encryption of all frames between access ports
Automatic assignment of public addresses to internal hosts

stem: What is the recommended treatment for switch access ports that are not in use?
explanation: An unused port that is still enabled is an open door: anyone who reaches the wall jack gets a working Layer 2 connection. Administratively shutting the port and parking it in a dedicated unused VLAN removes both the physical path and any chance of landing in a production VLAN.

choices.text: Shut the port down and assign it to an unused VLAN
Leave it enabled so new users can connect without a change request
Trunk it to every VLAN so it is ready for any device
Set it to dynamic auto so it negotiates the correct VLAN later

stem: What does a DHCP starvation attack accomplish before the attacker introduces a rogue DHCP server?
explanation: The attacker floods DHCPDISCOVER messages with fabricated MAC addresses until the legitimate pool has no addresses left. Clients then fail to get a lease and are willing to accept one from the rogue server, which hands out an address whose default gateway points at the attacker.

choices.text: It exhausts the legitimate DHCP pool with bogus requests so clients accept a rogue server's lease
It floods the CAM table so the switch forwards frames out every port
It poisons the ARP cache of the default gateway
It inserts double-tagged frames to reach another VLAN

stem: Which command blocks further login attempts for 60 seconds after five failures within 30 seconds?
explanation: `login block-for 60 attempts 5 within 30` enables the IOS login-blocking feature: after five failures in a 30-second window, all logins are refused for 60 seconds regardless of source. It turns an unlimited brute-force attempt into a rate-limited one.

stem: Why is `no ip source-route` commonly part of a router hardening baseline?
explanation: With source routing enabled, a sender can specify the path a packet takes through the network, which lets an attacker steer traffic around filters or probe internal addresses. Disabling it makes the router drop packets carrying the source-route option.

choices.text: It drops packets that try to dictate their own path through the network
It prevents the router from being used as a DHCP relay
It disables routing between directly connected subnets
It blocks all ICMP redirect messages

stem: Which command disables the router's embedded HTTP management server?
explanation: `no ip http server` turns off the cleartext web interface, and on platforms that support it `no ip http secure-server` removes the HTTPS one as well. If nobody uses browser-based management, leaving it running only widens the attack surface.

stem: Why do some hardening baselines disable Cisco Discovery Protocol on ports facing untrusted networks?
explanation: CDP advertisements include the device model, IOS version, and management addresses, all of which help an attacker choose an exploit and find a target. Disabling it on edge ports keeps that inventory out of reach while internal management links can still use it.

choices.text: CDP advertisements disclose device model, software version, and management addresses
CDP consumes enough bandwidth to starve production traffic
CDP prevents VLAN trunking from forming
CDP disables spanning tree on the port

stem: Which DNS record type maps a fully qualified hostname to an IPv4 address?
explanation: An A record holds the IPv4 address for a name, and it is the record a resolver returns for a normal forward lookup. IPv6 addresses live in AAAA records, which is why the two are often configured side by side for dual-stack hosts.

stem: Which DNS record type delegates authority for a zone to a set of name servers?
explanation: NS records name the authoritative servers for a zone, and the parent zone holds them for each delegation. That is how a resolver follows the chain from the root down to the server that can answer authoritatively for a domain.

stem: Which DNS record type carries free-form text used for sender policy and domain ownership verification?
explanation: TXT records hold arbitrary strings, and that flexibility made them the standard carrier for SPF, DKIM, and DMARC policy as well as for proving domain control to cloud providers. Nothing in the record format constrains the content; the consuming service defines the syntax.

stem: Which DNS record type lets a client discover both the hostname and the port for a specific service in a domain?
explanation: SRV records pair a service and protocol with a target host, a port, and a priority and weight, so clients do not need a hardcoded port. Directory services and voice deployments rely on them to locate domain controllers and SIP endpoints.

stem: How many TCP connections does a standard FTP session use, and what is the control connection's port?
explanation: FTP separates signalling from data: a control connection stays open on TCP 21 for commands and replies, and a separate data connection is opened for each transfer. Firewalls that inspect only port 21 therefore miss the transfer itself.

choices.text: Two connections, with the control connection on TCP 21
One connection, using TCP 21 for both commands and data
Two connections, with the control connection on UDP 21
Three connections, with the control connection on TCP 20

stem: In FTP active mode, how is the data connection established?
explanation: The client sends a PORT command naming an address and port, and the server opens the data connection back to the client from TCP 20. That inbound connection from the server is exactly what a client-side firewall blocks, which is why passive mode exists.

choices.text: The server initiates a connection from TCP 20 to a port the client specified
The client initiates a connection to TCP 20 on the server
Both sides send data over the existing control connection
The server sends data over UDP 20 without a handshake

stem: Which TCP port does implicit FTPS use by default?
explanation: Implicit FTPS begins TLS as soon as the connection opens on TCP 990, so there is no cleartext command phase at all. Explicit FTPS instead starts on port 21 and upgrades with AUTH TLS, which is why the two variants need different firewall rules.

stem: How does explicit FTPS establish encryption when it starts on port 21?
explanation: Explicit FTPS opens a normal FTP control connection and then the client issues AUTH TLS, which upgrades that session to TLS before any credentials are sent. Because the upgrade is negotiated in-band, the default port stays 21 and existing firewall rules keep working.

choices.text: The client issues AUTH TLS on the port 21 control connection and the session upgrades to TLS
The server immediately requires TLS on port 990
The client opens a separate SSH tunnel on port 22
The data connection is encrypted while commands remain in cleartext
